doc.title: Wendy Oxenhorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 22, 2026

title: The blind legend and Meals on Wheels
summary: Ron Carter flagged a nearly blind legend living on M&Ms; she persuaded him to try Meals on Wheels and his energy and gigs came back.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: It’s beyond. And we know all the earlier racism, everyone knows the clubs, the labels, the record companies, we know so many things that went down back then. There was one story that really stands out in my early moments, and I’ll segue into the Great Night in Harlem and answer your question, but there was a legend who – I think it was Ron Carter who came to me and said, “I ran into someone at the airport and he didn’t have a seeing eye cane but he was blind as a bat, he really couldn’t see where he was going.” And this was like a serious legend who had recorded with everyone. He said, “I asked him where he was coming back from and he had been in Greece for one night for five hundred dollars.” And Ron Carter took him in his car and drove him two hours back to his home in Jersey or Pennsylvania. And he said, “You’ve got to get in touch with this guy, he needs us.” So I called him and we started speaking and he said – “I don’t need any help, lady.” You know. So we got to the subject of how is he eating, how is he shopping. He can’t drive. So he lived a block away from a 7-Eleven and he was drinking those cans of Ensure and M&Ms, eating M&Ms. So I found out he’d been doing that for over a year. So I suggested, because we didn’t have a lot of money then but I suggested Meals on Wheels. And he was like, “I don’t need any kind of help, lady” and he hung up on me. And I was like oh man. So I called him back the next day and I said, “Listen,” I said, I worried about you all night. I didn’t sleep you know. I said, “We got tight on the phone, we were telling, we were comparing stories.” I was telling of some of the old man train station blues stories and we were laughing. And I said, “I’m going to be worrying about you now.” And I was talking into his machine. He didn’t pick up. And then all of a sudden the receiver picks up, he goes, “Wendy, I don’t want you to worry about me.” I said, “Well then I’m going to ask you one favor in our relationship would you promise me, would you try, just once would you try, this places delivers good meals like twice a day, lunch and dinner. Just try it once. Okay? Just so that I’ll sleep.” You know. So he agreed. He called up later the next day after they made their first visit. And he was just like over the moon. He said it had been so long since I had like real food. And he was just like so full of energy and happiness, and he loved the woman who delivered it. She sat and talked with him. He had no company.
